notes: Contact: Priya Nair (VP Eng) + Eli Turner (Head of ML infra)
Primary pain: inconsistent 95/99th latency during RTB bid windows leads to dropped bids and revenue loss.
Targets: p95 < 75ms for reranking path (single-turn), sustain 2k qps with <120ms p95 for embeddings pipeline, cost target <$0.0008 per inference on average.
Current infra: mix of cloud GPU pools + on-prem X86 servers running Triton; custom request router shards by campaign.
Model preferences: prefer open LLM variants for reranker (Llama2-13B / quantized) and specialized tiny reranker for hot-path; will consider Redwood-verified quantized variants.
Routing/fallback needs: want smart routing by latency SLO and model cost tier; automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variant on overload.
Optimization interests: aggressive batching at non-peak, adaptive batching during bursts, prefix/KV cache for frequent campaign prompts, 4-bit/8-bit quantization evaluation for 13B class models.
Perf benchmarking asks: need token/sec and latency curves across seq lengths 16/64/128; tail-latency (p95/p99) under 4 concurrent burst profiles; guidance on batch vs non-batch SLO tradeoffs.
Security/compliance: strict retention policy (30 days for live request logs), must support audit logging and KMS; data residency: US only for EU customers but primary ops NA.
Quote from Priya: 'We need predictability during the 100ms auction window — if inference slips, we lose bids.'
Internal note: likely conversion if Dedicated POC confirms 30-40% cost reduction via caching+quantization without p95 regressions.
